title: Constructing Triangles and Cross Sections
seo_title: Grade 7 Constructing Triangles and Cross Sections Worksheets: Triangle Inequality and Slicing Solids
standard_text: Draw geometric shapes with given conditions, focusing on constructing triangles from three measures of angles or sides, noticing when the conditions determine a unique triangle, more than one triangle, or no triangle. Describe the two-dimensional figures that result from slicing three-dimensional figures, as in plane sections of right rectangular prisms and right rectangular pyramids.
meta_desc: Free Grade 7 constructing triangles worksheets: the triangle inequality, angle sums, when conditions give one, many or no triangles, classifying triangles, and cross sections of prisms, pyramids, cylinders and cones. 100 practice questions with an answer key.
key_big: The two shorter sides must add to more than the longest. The angles always add to 180°.
key_sub: Three sides that work give exactly one triangle; three angles give one shape in many sizes. A slice parallel to a base copies the base.
body_html:
When do sides make a triangle?

The two shorter sides must add to more than the longest side. 3, 4 and 5 work (3 + 4 = 7 > 5). 2, 3 and 6 do not (2 + 3 = 5 < 6). The angles of every triangle add to 180°.

What you are givenHow many triangles
Three sides (that work)exactly one
Two sides and the angle between themexactly one
Two angles and the side between themexactly one
Three angles that add to 180°many (same shape, different sizes)
Sides where the two shorter add to the longest or lessnone
Example

Two sides are 5 in. and 8 in. What can the third side be?

More than 8 − 5 = 3.

Less than 8 + 5 = 13.

Answer: between 3 in. and 13 in.

Cross sections

A cross section is the flat shape you see when you slice a solid.

SliceCross section
Prism or cylinder, parallel to the basesame shape as the base
Pyramid or cone, parallel to the basesmaller copy of the base
Pyramid or cone, straight down through the toptriangle
Any slice of a spherecircle

Common mistakes

  • Checking only one pair of sides: always use the two shortest.
  • Thinking three angles give one triangle: they give one shape in many sizes.
  • Saying every slice of a prism looks like the base: a slice through the side can be a rectangle.

faq.q: How do you know if three lengths make a triangle?
faq.a: Add the two shorter lengths. If the sum is more than the longest length, they make a triangle. 3, 4, 5 work; 2, 3, 6 do not.

faq.q: Do three angles make a unique triangle?
faq.a: No. If they add to 180°, they fix the shape, but you can draw the triangle in many sizes.
The flat shape you get when you slice a solid. Slicing a rectangular prism parallel to its base gives a rectangle like the base.

faq.q: What cross sections can a pyramid have?
faq.a: A slice parallel to the base is a smaller copy of the base. A slice straight down through the top point is a triangle.

sets.title: Can these sides make a triangle?

items.q: Can sides of 3 cm, 4 cm and 5 cm make a triangle?
c: Only if two sides are equal
Only if it is a right triangle
items.e: Add the two shorter sides: 3 + 4 = 7. 7 > 5, so they make a triangle.

items.q: Can sides of 2 cm, 3 cm and 6 cm make a triangle?
c: Only if two sides are equal
Only if it is a right triangle
items.e: Add the two shorter sides: 2 + 3 = 5. 5 < 6, so the sides cannot meet.

items.q: Can sides of 5 cm, 5 cm and 10 cm make a triangle?
c: Only if it is a right triangle
Only if two sides are equal
items.e: Add the two shorter sides: 5 + 5 = 10. 10 = 10, so the sides lie flat and do not make a triangle.

items.q: Can sides of 7 cm, 8 cm and 9 cm make a triangle?
c: Only if two sides are equal
Only if it is a right triangle
items.e: Add the two shorter sides: 7 + 8 = 15. 15 > 9, so they make a triangle.

items.q: Can sides of 1 cm, 2 cm and 4 cm make a triangle?

Only if it is a right triangle
items.e: Add the two shorter sides: 1 + 2 = 3. 3 < 4, so the sides cannot meet.

Only if two sides are equal
items.e: Add the two shorter sides: 6 + 6 = 12. 12 > 6, so they make a triangle.

items.q: Two sides of a triangle are 4 m and 7 m. Which length could the third side be?
items.e: The third side must be more than 7 − 4 = 3 and less than 4 + 7 = 11.

items.q: Two sides of a triangle are 5 m and 9 m. Which length could the third side be?
items.e: The third side must be more than 9 − 5 = 4 and less than 5 + 9 = 14.

items.q: Two sides of a triangle are 3 m and 10 m. Which length could the third side be?
items.e: The third side must be more than 10 − 3 = 7 and less than 3 + 10 = 13.

items.q: Two sides of a triangle are 6 m and 6 m. Which length could the third side be?
items.e: The third side must be more than 6 − 6 = 0 and less than 6 + 6 = 12.

items.q: Two sides of a triangle are 5 in. and 8 in. What are all the possible lengths x of the third side?
items.e: x must be greater than 8 − 5 = 3 and less than 5 + 8 = 13.

items.q: Two sides of a triangle are 2 in. and 9 in. What are all the possible lengths x of the third side?
items.e: x must be greater than 9 − 2 = 7 and less than 2 + 9 = 11.

items.q: What is the rule for three side lengths to make a triangle?
c: The two shorter sides must add to more than the longest side
All three sides must be equal
The longest side must be more than the other two together
items.e: This is the triangle inequality. If the short sides add to exactly the longest, the triangle is flat.

items.q: How many different triangles can you make with sides 5 cm, 6 cm and 7 cm?
items.e: Three side lengths that work fix the shape: exactly one triangle (copies are the same triangle).

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 50° and 60°. What is the third angle?
items.e: The angles of a triangle add to 180°: 180 − 50 − 60 = 70°.

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 90° and 45°. What is the third angle?
items.e: The angles of a triangle add to 180°: 180 − 90 − 45 = 45°.

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 30° and 30°. What is the third angle?

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 100° and 35°. What is the third angle?

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 25° and 65°. What is the third angle?

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 60° and 60°. What is the third angle?

items.q: Two angles of a triangle are 15° and 120°. What is the third angle?

items.q: How many triangles have angles 60°, 70° and 50°?
c: One triangle shape, but many sizes
items.e: 60 + 70 + 50 = 180, so the angles work. But angles do not fix the size: you can draw small or large triangles with these angles.

items.q: How many triangles have angles 90°, 60° and 40°?
items.e: 90 + 60 + 40 = 190, not 180, so no triangle has these angles.

items.q: How many triangles have angles 45°, 45° and 90°?
c: One triangle shape, but many sizes
items.e: 45 + 45 + 90 = 180. Many sizes are possible.
